newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: First Quantum invests C$40 mln in Zambia mine.
newsitem.headline: First Quantum invests C$40 mln in Zambia mine.

text.p: Canada's First Quantum Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday it would invest C$40 million in developing the recently re-opened Bwana Mkubwa copper mine in northern Zambian and planned to commence other mining operations in the country soon.

"First Quantum Minerals Ltd is investing Canadian $40 million in a new SXEW operation at Bwana Mkubwa near Ndola," company president Clive Newall told an investment conference organised by the Financial Times in the Zambian capital. SXEW is a technique which uses acid to recover copper.
First Quantum is due to start site preparations this month at the Bwana Mukubwa mine, which was closed in 1984 by Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines.

Feasibility studies conducted by Bateman Minerals and Industrial Ltd of South Africa have found the mine to have a tailings reserve of 8.4 million tonnes at 0.73 percent copper. First Quantum expects to start production by April 1998.

Newall also said First Quantum hoped to start preliminary work at ZCCM's Luanshya Division and Chambishi copper mine once negotiations with the Zambian government on the sale of ZCCM assets had been concluded.
First Quantum is among several international concerns that bid for ZCCM's Luanshya Division and Chambishi mine in February.

"At Luanshya, the Lufubu North and South areas comprise aproximately 58 square kilometres overlying lower Roan sediments which are known to be copper bearing. A major drilling operation is planned to commence as soon as possible," Newall said.
"Also at Launshya, there are substantial resources of acid soluble copper which will be the subject of a detailed feasibility study commencing immediately," he added.
Newall said the Chambishi south-east deposit was potentially very large but had been subjected to only limited drilling.

"It is my view that once the privatisation of ZCCM is complete and the new owners have had an opportunity to thoroughly evaluate all drill hole and other exploration data, many more exploration targets will be identified on the ZCCM licence area," he aid.
Other bidders for Luanshya Division were the Binani Group, Sterlite Industries, Straits Resources, Reunion Mining and AUR Resources.
Bidders for Chambishi included Sterlite Industries, Farrel Financial Ltd and AUR Resources.
Newall said that, despite the decline in Zambia's mining output over the years, international mining houses were confident in the country's mining potential.

"The international mining community has recognised that the decline in copper and cobalt production from the Copperbelt is not solely due to depletion of reserves. Since nationalisation in 1969 there has been a dearth of finance available to delineate further reserves or to finance changes in mining as and when they become neccessary," he said.
"The international industry now believes that, with new investment and management, some of these mines can return to, or even exceed, historic profitable production levels," he said.
Zambia's copper output has dwindled from a high of around 755,000 tonnes in 1969 to 313,900 tonnes last year.
